metadata.author: V2 expansion (subagent draft)
metadata.key_test: Does a moderate P1 absorb a catastrophic economic shock (the 2001-2002 default and ~20% GDP collapse) WITHOUT territorial fragmentation or sustained political violence -- democracy holding through five presidents in two weeks? Economic crisis decoupled from state breakup. Pairs against Venezuela (case22, crisis WITH capture).
metadata.notes: Reference-based record: indicators resolved live via mi.datasource. resolved_scores carry MI v2 re-scored pillars (pre 2000, post 2024).

pre_event.event_description: Argentina on the eve of its 2001-2002 sovereign default and convertibility collapse -- then the world's largest sovereign default -- with GDP down ~20% (1998-2002), unemployment ~21.5%, poverty above 45%.

context.backstop_details: IMF program involvement but no external backstop preventing default.

Argentina.notes: Indicators resolved via mi.datasource (Argentina, 2000 -> 2024). Test of complexity-capacity matching and the stability claim: moderate institutional P1 absorbing a maximal economic shock without fragmentation/civil war.

a_trajectory_ranking.prediction: Institutional continuity; Tier 2 maintained despite economic shock and mild MI decline.
a_trajectory_ranking.basis: Pre-P1 0.502 (moderate) is high enough to absorb the shock without institutional collapse; economic pillars (P2/P4) take the hit, P1 holds.
a_trajectory_ranking.falsification_condition: Argentina drops below Tier 2 / suffers institutional (not merely economic) collapse.

b_violence.prediction: Elevated unrest risk around the crisis peak, but no sustained political violence or civil war.
b_violence.agency_note: Mod8: this predicts RISK, not AGENCY.

c_convergence.prediction: N/A (single entity); self-trajectory: shock then recovery.

d_failure_dimension.prediction: Stress concentrates on economic capacity (P4) and openness/distribution (P2); institutional P1 holds flat.
d_failure_dimension.note: Most exposed to post-hoc coding bias.
d_failure_dimension.falsification_condition: P1 collapses / failure concentrates on institutions.

e_fragment_count.prediction: No territorial fragmentation; state stays intact.

f_reversal_risk.prediction: Elevated executive-turnover risk (multiple presidents) but NO democratic reversal / military coup -- constitutional succession holds.
f_reversal_risk.falsification_condition: Military coup or extra-constitutional seizure of power.

g_suppression_mechanism.classification: N/A -- not a suppressed-fragmentation suppression-tier case.

h_substate_turbulence.prediction: Provincial fiscal/social turbulence (provincial quasi-currencies, piquetero movements) but contained and reabsorbed.
h_substate_turbulence.falsification_condition: Provincial breakaway or sustained sub-state armed turbulence.

Argentina.outcome_summary: P1 0.502->0.489 (near-flat); MI 0.694->0.630 (Tier 2 maintained). Dec 2001 saw ~39 dead in riots and five presidents in two weeks, the world's then-largest sovereign default, GDP down ~20% -- yet constitutional succession held, no coup, no territorial fragmentation, and democracy continued through 2003 elections and beyond. Economic pillars absorbed the hit (P2 0.745->0.441; P4 0.834->0.720).
key_events: five presidents in two weeks (constitutional succession)

a_trajectory.explanation: Institutional continuity through a maximal economic shock, as predicted.

b_violence.evidence: Dec 2001 riots (~39 dead) then stabilization; no civil war.
b_violence.explanation: Moderate unrest risk realized and bounded; no sustained violence.
b_violence.data_refreshed: 2026-06-28: focus=Argentina pre-P1=0.502 -> LOW risk (MI v1, anchored)

d_failure_dimension.evidence: P2 collapsed 0.745->0.441 and P4 fell 0.834->0.720 while P1 held near-flat.
d_failure_dimension.explanation: Economic pillars absorbed the shock as predicted; institutional P1 held. Post-hoc dimension call coded PARTIAL.
d_failure_dimension.computed_config: Argentina: P4=0.83, P2=0.74, P3=0.74, P5=0.65, P1=0.50 | all pillars >= median -> no binding vulnerability (management-load/high-capacity case; relatively-lowest P1=0.50)

e_fragment_count.data_refreshed: 2026-06-28 (outcome judgment preserved; safeguard re-evaluated on real data)

f_reversal_risk.evidence: Five presidents in two weeks via constitutional succession; no military coup -- a notable break from Argentina's coup history.
f_reversal_risk.explanation: Executive turnover realized; democratic reversal avoided, exactly as predicted.
f_reversal_risk.data_refreshed: 2026-06-28 (outcome judgment preserved; safeguard re-evaluated on real data)

g_suppression.data_refreshed: 2026-06-28 (outcome judgment preserved; safeguard re-evaluated on real data)

h_turbulence.evidence: Provincial quasi-currencies (patacones, etc.) and piquetero movements emerged and were reabsorbed.
h_turbulence.explanation: Contained sub-state fiscal/social turbulence as predicted.
h_turbulence.data_refreshed: 2026-06-28 (outcome judgment preserved; safeguard re-evaluated on real data)

analysis.overall_assessment: Clean 'crisis without state breakup' confirmation: a moderate P1 absorbed a catastrophic economic shock with institutional and territorial continuity, contrasting sharply with Venezuela's crisis-with-capture (case22).
analysis.what_this_case_uniquely_reveals: Economic catastrophe and political fragmentation are decoupled: a sufficient institutional floor (moderate P1) lets a state survive a maximal economic shock without breaking up or abandoning constitutional rule.
